title: Move "allowed to use" to the Permissions Policy spec?
body:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#allowed-to-use is a thin wrapper around Permissions Policy's [is feature enabled in document for origin](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-permissions-policy/#is-feature-enabled). I don't think having HTML maintain this wrapper buys us much.

I believe "allowed to use"'s location in HTML in historical:

1. Originally, HTML defined `allowfullscreen=""`, `allowpaymentrequest=""`, and `allowusermedia=""`. So "allowed to use" was some logic checking those HTML-defined attributes.

1. Feature Policy (now Permissions Policy) defined `allow=""`, and HTML's "allowed to use" was added to wrap that in addition to the other 3.

1. Over time, we removed `allowpaymentrequest=""` and `allowusermedia=""` from the platform, so now "allowed to use" was a wrapper around `allowfullscreen=""` (defined in HTML) and `allow=""` (defined in Feature Policy).

1. Eventually Feature/Permissions Policy took over the processing model for `allowfullscreen=""`, making HTML's "allowed to use" just a wrapper around the Permissions Policy algorithm like it is today.

I confirmed with @clelland that moving "allowed to use" makes sense to him. Any thoughts or objections from other folks?
